scores.criterion: Introduction and background (assembly language, architecture, system calls, project overview, assumptions)
scores.justification: The overview of IA-32 architecture and memory segmentation is somewhat brief, and Section 1.3 has minor formatting inconsistencies in its bullet points. However, Tables 1 and 2 clearly and accurately map specific x86 registers and Linux int 0x80 system calls (like poll and nanosleep) directly to their roles in the SmartSignal project.

scores.criterion: Research and critical analysis (relevance of assembly, areas of use, cyber security / forensics / malware analysis, case studies, practical demonstration)
scores.justification: Section 2.2.1 (Embedded and Real-Time Systems) fails to discuss embedded systems at all, instead accidentally pasting the exact paragraph from Section 2.1 verbatim. Despite this major editing gap, the practical reverse engineering demonstration in Section 2.4—stripping the SmartSignal binary, profiling int 0x80 calls, disassembling handle_ped, and binary patching—is outstanding.

The narrative in Section 3.2 contains slight confusion when describing how emergency overrides and pedestrian requests extend the amber versus all-red phases. Nevertheless, the system functionalities (Table 5), six-phase state model (Table 6), flowcharts, and memory layout in the .data and .bss sections (Table 7) are thoroughly and logically documented.

scores.criterion: Implementation of the required constructs (ADD/SUB, loops, conditional and unconditional jumps, input validation) with explanation
scores.justification: Only selected code snippets are included in the report text while the full 1,700-line source code is referenced as an external file, leaving some helper routines like is_allred unshown. Still, the provided NASM excerpts excellently demonstrate ADD/SUB arithmetic, LOOP and DEC/JNZ constructs, conditional/unconditional jumps, raw terminal ioctl configuration, and range-checked input validation.

The test log in Table 9 summarizes expected and actual results briefly without specifying detailed pre-conditions or exact memory/register state checks. However, the 18 test cases cover strong edge cases (such as /dev/null EOF handling and Ctrl+C signal restoration), and the user manual provides comprehensive build instructions for both x86 and ARM/QEMU alongside complete screenshots.

The conclusion ends abruptly mid-sentence ("adjusting green time depending on"), several references (Barr & Massa, VirusTotal, Yiu) are not cited in the text, and Appendix B.2 contradicts B.1 by showing evidence for a "cat" command prompt instead of the traffic light simulator. While APA formatting and general structure are otherwise neat, these presentation and proofreading lapses significantly lower the mark.
